bull.t: Data-center growth and server share gains
bull.b: Rapid data-center growth is strengthening AMD’s position in an attractive, expanding compute market. Record EPYC adoption and share gains across cloud and enterprise customers can support recurring platform deployments, broaden the revenue base, and reinforce AMD’s relevance across future server cycles.

bull.t: Conservative balance sheet and improved profitability
bull.b: Low leverage gives AMD substantial financial flexibility to fund product development, capacity commitments, and strategic initiatives without placing excessive pressure on cash flows. The accompanying improvement in profitability and returns on equity indicates that growth is translating into stronger earnings power.

bull.t: Strategic AI partnerships and ecosystem expansion
bull.b: Large, multi-year AI commitments can validate AMD’s accelerator roadmap and create durable demand beyond individual product launches. Deployments with major technology platforms may also improve software adoption, customer references, and ecosystem scale, strengthening AMD’s competitive position over several years.

bear.b: The sharp gaming decline exposes AMD to weakness in console shipment cycles and consumer graphics demand, reducing diversification while data-center investment accelerates. Continued softness could weigh on segment mix, limit near-term revenue stability, and leave more earnings dependent on a smaller number of growth markets.

Strong demand cannot fully convert into revenue if wafers, substrates, back-end capacity, or new-node yields remain constrained. Ramp execution for Helios and 2nm products could delay customer deployments, increase costs, and pressure early margins, making operational delivery a material execution risk.

Aggressive investment is strategically important but raises the cost base faster than some operating benefits may emerge. If AI product adoption or software monetization takes longer than expected, elevated research and go-to-market spending could restrain operating leverage and reduce the durability of margin expansion.
